claim: The Tbx21Cre mouse expresses cre selectively in M/T cells.
source: The Tbx21Cre mouse expresses cre selectively in M/T cells, and the Rosa26DTA mouse expresses diphtheria toxin (DTA) upon cre-mediated recombination, which triggers the death of M/T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text describing the genetic strategy.

claim: The Rosa26DTA mouse expresses diphtheria toxin (DTA) upon cre-mediated recombination, which triggers the death of M/T cells.
source: The Tbx21Cre mouse expresses cre selectively in M/T cells, and the Rosa26DTA mouse expresses diphtheria toxin (DTA) upon cre-mediated recombination, which triggers the death of M/T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text describing the genetic strategy and references Figure 1B.

claim: The number of tdTomato positive M/T cells observed in the OB of adult Tbx21::Ai9 mice was similar to that previously reported.
source: The number of (tdTomato (tdT) positive cells) tdT +M/T cells that we observed in the OB of adult Tbx21::Ai9 mice was similar to that previously reported (Benson et al., 1984; Richard et al., 2010), and by P3 the vast majority, if not all, M/T cells expressed tdT in Tbx21::Ai9 mice at P3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Benson et al., 1984; Richard et al., 2010).

claim: By P3 the vast majority, if not all, M/T cells expressed tdT in Tbx21::Ai9 mice.
source: The number of (tdTomato (tdT) positive cells) tdT +M/T cells that we observed in the OB of adult Tbx21::Ai9 mice was similar to that previously reported (Benson et al., 1984; Richard et al., 2010), and by P3 the vast majority, if not all, M/T cells expressed tdT in Tbx21::Ai9 mice at P3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tbx21::DTA mice survive and reach adulthood without any gross differences from their wild-type siblings.
source: Tbx21::DTA mice survive and reach adulthood without any gross differences from their wild-type siblings (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The OB volume of Tbx21::DTA mice was reduced to half.
source: Although the OB volume of Tbx21::DTA mice was reduced to half, the typical OB layer organization was mostly preserved (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The typical OB layer organization was mostly preserved in Tbx21::DTA mice.
source: Although the OB volume of Tbx21::DTA mice was reduced to half, the typical OB layer organization was mostly preserved (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: A small number of Tbr2+ cells remained in the mitral cell layer (MCL) and external plexiform layer (EPL) after cell ablation.
source: Interestly, using antibodies against the Tbr2 protein (a marker for M/T cells), we identified a small number of Tbr2+ cells remaining in the mitral cell layer (MCL) and external plexiform layer (EPL) after cell ablation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: A single molecule of DTA is sufficient to kill a cell.
source: Previous works have demonstrated that DTA is extremely potent, and that a single molecule of DTA is sufficient to kill a cell (Yamaizumi et al., 1978).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yamaizumi et al., 1978.

claim: The recombination of the loxP-tdT transgene is more sensitive to cre than the loxP-DTA transgene.
source: These observations are consistent with the recombination of the loxP-tdT transgene being more sensitive to cre than the loxP-DTA transgene, a phenomenon that has been routinely reported in the literature (Becher et al., 2018; Kurachi et al., 2019; Madisen et al., 2010; Song and Palmiter, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations (Becher et al., 2018; Kurachi et al., 2019; Madisen et al., 2010; Song and Palmiter, 2018).

claim: Approximately 25% of M/T cells remained at P10 in Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice compared with wild type mice.
source: In Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice, approximately 25% of the M/T cells remained at P10 (9,606.5±1,229.7; n=4),~3% at P21 (1,024.8±282.3; n=9), and ~1% at P120 (437.6±119.2; n=8) compared with wild type (Tbx21) mice at P120 (38,546.8±2,912.2; n=3).
evidence: This is stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: Approximately 3% of M/T cells remained at P21 in Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice compared with wild type mice.
source: In Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice, approximately 25% of the M/T cells remained at P10 (9,606.5±1,229.7; n=4),~3% at P21 (1,024.8±282.3; n=9), and ~1% at P120 (437.6±119.2; n=8) compared with wild type (Tbx21) mice at P120 (38,546.8±2,912.2; n=3).
evidence: This is stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: Approximately 1% of M/T cells remained at P120 in Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice compared with wild type mice.
source: In Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice, approximately 25% of the M/T cells remained at P10 (9,606.5±1,229.7; n=4),~3% at P21 (1,024.8±282.3; n=9), and ~1% at P120 (437.6±119.2; n=8) compared with wild type (Tbx21) mice at P120 (38,546.8±2,912.2; n=3).
evidence: This is stated with specific quantitative data.

claim: At P10, ~95% of the remaining M/T cells had a single apical dendrite innervating a single glomerulus.
source: At P10, ~95% of the remaining M/T cells had a single apical dendrite innervating a single glomerulus (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells proceeds normally despite a progressive drastic reduction in the density of M/T cells.
source: These results indicate that the refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells proceeds normally despite a progressive drastic reduction in the density of M/T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Only 3% of the M/T cells remained in Tbx21::iDTR::Ai9 mice at P120 compared with wild type mice after DT injection at P60.
source: DT injections into P60 Tbx21::iDTR::Ai9 mice were analyzed two months later (P120), and only 3% of the M/T cells remained compared with the wild type (Tbx21::Ai9) mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: In Tbx21::iDTR mice, 48% of the remaining M/T cells branched to several glomeruli.
source: Surprisingly, in Tbx21::iDTR mice, 48% of the remaining M/T cells branched to several glomeruli (Figure 2F1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2F1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: By P120, 36% of remaining M/T cells in Tbx21::DTA mice projected their apical dendrite into multiple glomeruli.
source: Interestingly, whereas in Tbx21::DTA mice the apical dendrite of remaining M/T cells innervated a single glomerulus at P10, we also observed that by P120, 36% of remaining M/T cells projected their apical dendrite into multiple glomeruli, as in the Tbx21::iDTR mice (Figure 2D1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell ablation performed in 6-month-old Tbx21::iDTR mice (P180) showed that 45% of remaining M/T cells branched to several glomeruli.
source: We also investigated whether the plasticity of the apical dendrite is reduced with age. Cell ablation performed in 6-mo--old Tbx21::iDTR mice (P180) showed that 45% of remaining M/T cells branched to several glomeruli, a percentage comparable to that of animals in which ablation was performed at P60, indicating that the ability of M/T cells to experience drastic morphological changes in their dendrites does not decrease with age (Figure 2G1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2G1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The ability of M/T cells to experience drastic morphological changes in their dendrites does not decrease with age.
source: We also investigated whether the plasticity of the apical dendrite is reduced with age. Cell ablation performed in 6-mo--old Tbx21::iDTR mice (P180) showed that 45% of remaining M/T cells branched to several glomeruli, a percentage comparable to that of animals in which ablation was performed at P60, indicating that the ability of M/T cells to experience drastic morphological changes in their dendrites does not decrease with age (Figure 2G1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing ablation at P60 vs P180.

claim: The tuft length of M/T cells in Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR was increased compared to apical dendrite tuft in control Tbx21.
source: The tuft length of M/T cells in Tbx21::DTA (early postnatal cell ablation), and Tbx21::iDTR (cell ablation at P60 and P120) was increased compared to apical dendrite tuft in control Tbx21 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A sufficient density of M/T cells are required for the maintenance of a normal mature morphology (one apical dendrite-one glomerulus).
source: These results indicate that a sufficient density of M/T cells are required for the maintenance of a normal mature morphology (one apical dendrite-one glomerulus), suggesting that structural plasticity is not locked even six months after M/T cells acquired their mature morphology.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Structural plasticity is not locked even six months after M/T cells acquired their mature morphology.
source: These results indicate that a sufficient density of M/T cells are required for the maintenance of a normal mature morphology (one apical dendrite-one glomerulus), suggesting that structural plasticity is not locked even six months after M/T cells acquired their mature morphology.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: In wild type animals, there are ~2000 glomeruli, and each glomerulus is innervated by around 40–50 M/T cells.
source: In wild type animals, there are ~2000 glomeruli, and each glomerulus is innervated by around 40–50 M/T cells.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about the olfactory system.

claim: When half (10 μg/kg) of the DT dose was injected, the fraction of remaining M/T cells was 25% (~10,000 cells) compared to wild type mice (~40,000 cells).
source: When we injected half (10 μg/kg) of the DT dose used in our previous experiments, the fraction of remaining M/T cells was 25% (~10,000 cells) compared to wild type mice (~40,000 cells; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: In animals injected with half the DT dose, ~40% of the M/T cells still projected to multiple glomeruli.
source: However, in these animals, ~40% of the M/T cells still projected to multiple glomeruli, a similar percentage as in the animals with higher doses of DT in which the vast majority of M/T cells were ablated (Figure 2H1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2H1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The branching of M/T dendrites into multiple glomeruli does not simply occur because nearby glomeruli are empty.
source: These results suggest that the branching of M/T dendrites into multiple glomeruli does not simply occur because nearby glomeruli are empty.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the half-dose DT experiment.

claim: In wild type animals with a full set of M/T cells, a small percentage of M/T cells still innervate more than one glomerulus.
source: In addition, it is important to emphasize that even in wild type animals with a full set of M/T cells, a small percentage of M/T cells still innervate more than one glomerulus (Lin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Lin et al., 2000.

claim: The innervation of multiple glomeruli by M/T cells is not simply due to the presence of empty glomeruli.
source: Together, these observations suggest that the innervation of multiple glomeruli by M/T cells is not simply due to the presence of empty glomeruli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple observations.

claim: The ability of M/T cells to grow new dendrites and to project them to multiple glomeruli is not restricted to neonatal stages and can be induced in adults (6 mo old) mice.
source: These results indicate that the ability of M/T cells to grow new dendrites, and to project them to multiple glomeruli is not restricted to neonatal stages and that it can be induced in adults (6 mo old) mice, simply by reducing the density of their peer M/T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Only around half of the surviving M/T cells extended their apical dendrites toward several glomeruli, while the other half maintained a single dendrite that targeted a single glomerulus.
source: Interestingly, only around half of the surviving M/T cells their apical dendrites extended toward several glomeruli, while the other half maintained a single dendrite that targeted a single glomerulus.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: The ability of M/T cells to change their structure and grow dendrites into adjacent glomeruli may be restricted to specific subtypes of M/T types.
source: This observation suggests that the ability of M/T cells to change their structure and grow dendrites into adjacent glomeruli may be restricted to specific subtypes of M/T types.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that only half of M/T cells showed plasticity.

claim: M/T cells apical dendrite refinement occurs in the absence of sensory activity.
source: However, M/T cells apical dendrite refinement occurs in the absence of sensory activity (Lin et al., 2000; Ma et al., 2014), indicating that it is independent of input from OSNs.
evidence: This is stated with citations to Lin et al., 2000 and Ma et al., 2014.

claim: M/T cells apical dendrite refinement is independent of input from OSNs.
source: However, M/T cells apical dendrite refinement occurs in the absence of sensory activity (Lin et al., 2000; Ma et al., 2014), indicating that it is independent of input from OSNs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited studies.

claim: Sensory deprivation causes a decrease of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression in PG cells.
source: Sensory deprivation causes a decrease of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression in PG cells, and we confirmed that in these animals sensory deprivation was effective by TH immunostaining (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and confirmed by Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: M/T cells tuft length in sensory deprived OBs was reduced compared to apical dendrite tuft in control Tbx21::iDTR mice.
source: M/T cells tuft length in sensory deprived OBs was reduced compared to apical dendrite tuft in control Tbx21::iDTR mice (ablation at P60 and unmanipulated sensory input; Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The percentage of M/T cells innervating multiple glomeruli was similar regardless of whether the animals had a closed (39%) or open naris (44%) compared to the Tbx21::iDTR mice (48%).
source: However, the percentage of M/T cells innervating multiple glomeruli was similar regardless of whether the animals had a closed (39%) or open naris (44%) compared to the Tbx21::iDTR mice (48%; control mice; Figure 3B and E; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B, 3E, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Sensory stimuli are not essential for the expansion of M/T apical dendrites into multiple glomeruli in remaining M/T cells.
source: This result suggests that sensory stimuli are not essential for the expansion of M/T apical dendrites into multiple glomeruli in remaining M/T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the naris occlusion experiment.

claim: The overexpression of the Kir2.1 channel in remaining M/T cells did not cause statistically significant differences in the percentage of M/T innervating multiple glomeruli compared to remaining M/T cells in Tbx21::iDTR:DTA mice.
source: However, the overexpression of the Kir2.1 channel in remaining M/T cells did not cause statistically significant differences in the percentage of M/T innervating multiple glomeruli compared to remaining M/T cells in Tbx21::iDTR:DTA mice (Figure 3D and E; Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D, 3E, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The structural plasticity observed after reducing the total number of M/T cells in an animal is not regulated by the firing action potentials in the remaining cells.
source: These experiments demonstrate that the structural plasticity observed after reducing the total number of M/T cells in an animal is not regulated by the firing action potentials in the remaining cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Kir2.1 experiment.

claim: The observed structural plasticity may be regulated by other types of mechanisms (such as increased synaptic excitation) that do not require the M/T cells to fire action potentials in a physiological manner.
source: Instead, this experiment indicates that the observed structural plasticity may be regulated by other types of mechanisms (such as increased synaptic excitation) that do not require the M/T cells to fire action potentials in a physiological manner.
evidence: This is a speculation about alternative mechanisms.

claim: During development, axons from OSNs expressing the same odor receptor initially project to several neighboring glomeruli.
source: During development, axons from OSNs expressing the same odor receptor initially project to several neighboring glomeruli.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about olfactory development.

claim: In the first postnatal week, OSNs axons undergo a refinement process such that all OSNs expressing one receptor project into a single glomerulus and form a stereotypic odor map on the OB surface.
source: In the first postnatal week, OSNs axons undergo a refinement process such that all OSNs expressing one receptor project into a single glomerulus and form a stereotypic odor map on the OB surface (Mombaerts et al., 1996; Ressler et al., 1994; Vassar et al., 1994; Wang et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple studies.

claim: Once the odor map is established, it is maintained throughout the animal's lifespan, despite the constant turnover of OSNs.
source: Once the odor map is established, it is maintained throughout the animal's lifespan, despite the constant turnover of OSNs (Zou et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Zou et al., 2004.

claim: At P10 and P21 there were no differences in the targeting of M72 axons between Tbx21::M72 and Tbx21::DTA::M72 mice.
source: At P10 and P21 there were no differences in the targeting of M72 axons between Tbx21::M72 and Tbx21::DTA::M72 mice (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4C and E.

claim: A normal density of M/T cells is not necessary to refine OSN axons and odor map formation.
source: These results suggest that a normal density of M/T cells is not necessary to refine OSN axons and odor map formation, and it is consistent with previous works (Bulfone et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data and consistent with cited work.

claim: M72 axons projected to several glomeruli when OBs were analyzed 2 months after ablating M/T cells in adult Tbx21::iDTR::M72 mice.
source: Surprisingly, M72 axons projected to several glomeruli when OBs were analyzed 2 mo later (P120; Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D and E.

claim: In Tbx21::DTA mice, M72 axons projected into a single glomerulus at P10 and P21, but by P120 the M72 axons projected into multiple glomeruli.
source: Interestingly, whereas in Tbx21::DTA mice M72 axons projected into a single glomerulus at P10 and P21, we also observed that by P120 the M72 axons projected into multiple glomeruli, as in the Tbx21::iDTR mice (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D and E.

claim: The maintenance of the odor map on the OB surface depends on the presence of a sufficient density of M/T cells.
source: These results suggest that the maintenance of the odor map on the OB surface depends on the presence of a sufficient density of M/T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the M72 axon projection data.

claim: All Tbx21::DTA mice reached 80% accuracy when exposed to 5% cineole concentrations on their first trial.
source: Despite the massive loss of M/T cells and the disorganization of OB connectivity, all Tbx21::DTA mice reached 80% accuracy when exposed to 5% cineole (a chemical typically used for olfactory tests) concentrations on their first trial and even showed comparable accuracy to control Tbx21 mice at 0.5% cineole concentrations (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: Tbx21::DTA mice showed comparable accuracy to control Tbx21 mice at 0.5% cineole concentrations.
source: Despite the massive loss of M/T cells and the disorganization of OB connectivity, all Tbx21::DTA mice reached 80% accuracy when exposed to 5% cineole (a chemical typically used for olfactory tests) concentrations on their first trial and even showed comparable accuracy to control Tbx21 mice at 0.5% cineole concentrations (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A.

claim: Only 50% of Tbx21::iDTR animals successfully performed the go/no-go test on the first day of testing.
source: Whereas all the Tbx21::DTA mice (with early postnatal M/T ablation) succeeded in the go/no-go test, only 50% of Tbx21::iDTR (in which M/T ablation occurred as adults) successfully performed this paradigm on the first day of testing.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: 21% of Tbx21::iDTR mice were completely unable to perform the detection test at any time, even after training on this test for 3 weeks.
source: Of the remaining 50% of Tbx21::iDTR animals, 21% of the mice were completely unable to perform this detection test at any time, even after training on this test for 3 weeks.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: 29% of Tbx21::iDTR mice were eventually able to complete the test after 1 week of training.
source: The remaining 29% of Tbx21::iDTR mice were eventually able to complete the test after 1 week of training (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The assembly of an olfactory circuit with a reduced density of projection neurons in young animals (Tbx21::DTA mice) is compatible with preserved olfactory performance.
source: These observations indicate that the assembly of an olfactory circuit with a reduced density of projection neurons in young animals (Tbx21::DTA mice) is compatible with preserved olfactory performance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data.

claim: Reducing the density of M/T cells in an adult animal after the circuitry of its olfactory bulb was assembled normally (in Tbx21::iDTR mice) causes important deficits in olfactory performance.
source: In contrast, reducing the density of M/T cells in an adult animal after the circuitry of its olfactory bulb was assembled normally (in Tbx21::iDTR mice) causes important deficits in olfactory performance; however, in some cases, these deficits can be overcome after training.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data.

claim: Both Tbx21:DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice reached more than 80% accuracy criterion when exposed to pure molecules and binary mixtures (80/20::20/80) of cineole and eugenol.
source: Both Tbx21:DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice reached more than 80% accuracy criterion when exposed to pure molecules and binary mixtures (80/20::20/80; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Tbx21:DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice had difficulties discriminating between more similar binary mixtures (55/45::45/55) of cineole and eugenol.
source: However, they had difficulties discriminating between more similar binary mixtures (55/45::45/55).
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Tbx21::DTA mice failed to discriminate between carvone (+) and carvone (-), even when the odorants were presented as pure molecules.
source: Tbx21::DTA mice failed to discriminate between carvone (+) and carvone (-), even when the odorants were presented as pure molecules (not as mixtures).
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Tbx21::iDTR mice reached 80% accuracy in the discrimination test with pure molecules of carvone (+) and carvone (-).
source: In contrast, Tbx21::iDTR mice reached 80% accuracy in this version of the discrimination test with pure molecules (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Despite the reduced number of M/T cells and disorganization of their OBs in Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice, their olfactory system has a remarkable resilience that partially preserves their ability to smell.
source: These results suggest that despite the reduced number of M/T cells and disorganization of their OBs in Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice, their olfactory system has a remarkable resilience that partially preserves their ability to smell.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data.

claim: No apparent differences were observed in offspring nursing between both experimental Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice.
source: No apparent differences were observed in offspring nursing between both experimental Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice, indicating that this behavior was mostly preserved in females.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Only 16.67% of Tbx21::DTA males mated, compared to 63.63% of Tbx21::iDTR and 90.91% control Tbx21 animals.
source: Only 16.67% of Tbx21::DTA males mated, compared to 63.63% of Tbx21::iDTR and 90.91% control Tbx21 animals (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice did not initiate a fight when a wild type male or a male mouse from the same strain was introduced into its cage.
source: Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice did not initiate a fight when a wild type male or a male mouse from the same strain (Tbx::DTA or Tbx21::iDTR)was introduced into its cage.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: When Tbx21::DTA or Tbx21::iDTR male mice were the intruders, the resident wild type mice attacked them in 33% (Tbx21::DTA) and 28% (Tbx21::iDTR) of the cases, compared to 83% when the intruder was another wild type male mouse.
source: Moreover, when Tbx21::DTA or Tbx21::iDTR male mice were the intruders, the resident wild type mice attacked them in 33% (Tbx21::DTA) and 28% (Tbx21::iDTR) of the cases, compared to 83% when the intruder was another wild type male mouse (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5D.

claim: Only ~1.5% and 16% of M/T cells remained in the AOB of Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice and Tbx21::iDTR::Ai9 mice, respectively.
source: Wild type mice have around ~2000 M/T cells in their AOBs, while only ~1.5% and 16% of M/T cells remained in the AOB of Tbx21::DTA::Ai9 mice and Tbx21::iDTR::Ai9 mice, respectively (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: The drastically reduced number of AOB M/T cells in the Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice could explain their inability to engage in social behaviors such as a mating or aggression.
source: Thus, the drastically reduced number of AOB M/T cells in the Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice could explain their inability to engage in social behaviors such as a mating or aggression, suggesting that behaviors depending on the AOB are hard-wired, less plastic, and less resilient than the learned behaviors that depend on the main OB.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying behavioral deficits.

claim: Behaviors depending on the AOB are hard-wired, less plastic, and less resilient than the learned behaviors that depend on the main OB.
source: Thus, the drastically reduced number of AOB M/T cells in the Tbx21::DTA and Tbx21::iDTR mice could explain their inability to engage in social behaviors such as a mating or aggression, suggesting that behaviors depending on the AOB are hard-wired, less plastic, and less resilient than the learned behaviors that depend on the main OB.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the behavioral data.

claim: During development, each M/T cell extends several apical dendrites toward several glomeruli at the same time that OSN axons penetrate into the OB surface to form a glomerular structure.
source: During development, each M/T cell extends several apical dendrites toward several glomeruli at the same time that OSN axons penetrate into the OB surface to form a glomerular structure (Blanchart et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Blanchart et al., 2006.

claim: In the first week after birth, M/T cells undergo a refinement process where they end up with a single apical dendrite innervating a single glomerulus.
source: In the first week after birth, M/T cells undergo a refinement process where they end up with a single apical dendrite innervating a single glomerulus (Blanchart et al., 2006; Hinds, 1968a; Shepherd et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple studies.

claim: OSN axons are required both for glomerular formation and for the refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells.
source: It is known that OSN axons are required both for glomerular formation and for the refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells (Kobayakawa et al., 2007; Nishizumi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Kobayakawa et al., 2007 and Nishizumi et al., 2019.

claim: In the absence of OSN axons, M/T cells maintain an immature morphology with multiple apical dendrites even as animals mature and become adults.
source: In the absence of OSN axons, M/T cells maintain an immature morphology with multiple apical dendrites even as animals mature and become adults (Kobayakawa et al., 2007; Nishizumi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Kobayakawa et al., 2007 and Nishizumi et al., 2019.

claim: The refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells is independent of the sensory experience information driven by OSNs inputs.
source: Despite the requirement of OSN axons to form a glomerular structure, it has been described that the refinement of the apical dendrite of M/T cells is independent of the sensory experience information driven by OSNs inputs.
